description: Sync pages, blog posts and attached files from the Confluence Cloud spaces you choose. With Enforce ACL on, space permissions and page restrictions decide who can find each item.
opening: Sync pages, blog posts and their attached files from the Confluence Cloud spaces you select. Each page or blog post is one document, holding its text with the markup removed. Each attached file is its own document, linked to its page. Text from supported attachments is searchable when HydraDB can download and read the files. A page links to its parent page.

Space permissions and page view restrictions, including those inherited from parent pages, restrict search when Enforce ACL is on. An attached file follows only its space's permissions until its page has synced, so at first it can have a wider audience than its restricted page. Comments are not synced. Pages and files deleted in Confluence stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: Two levels apply. A space's view permissions decide who can read its pages, and a space open to all licensed users can be read by everyone who can query the collection. A page's own view restriction, and the restrictions of its restricted parent pages, narrow that further: a reader must meet every one of them. An attached file follows its page.
permissions.identity: A user's email address. Confluence groups are turned into their members' email addresses. This works only when the site shows user email addresses.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a space's permissions, or cannot resolve a page's restrictions, the connector reports a permission warning. A page restricted to a user whose email the site hides cannot be resolved.
notes: Reading a space's permissions needs the Space admin permission on that space.
A page whose restriction levels resolve to nobody, or have no reader in common, is hidden.
A file attached to a restricted page follows the space's permissions until its page has synced.
Space admins' access through their admin role is not recorded.
A restriction change that does not edit the page is checked on later syncs, not the first one. A restriction removed from a page can wait until the page is next edited.

connect.auth: Confluence uses an Atlassian account email and an Atlassian API token. The token carries that user's own space permissions.

credentials.name: base_url
credentials.text: Your Confluence Cloud address, for example `https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki`.

credentials.name: email
credentials.text: The Atlassian account email used to sign in.

credentials.name: api_token
credentials.text: An Atlassian API token for that account.

permissions.name: View space
permissions.text: required. Lists spaces and their pages.

permissions.name: View pages
permissions.text: required. Reads page and blog post text.

permissions.name: Space admin
permissions.text: optional, for search that follows Confluence permissions. Reads each space's permission list.

permissions.name: Browse users and groups
permissions.text: optional, for search that follows Confluence permissions. Turns groups into their members' emails and users into emails.

connect.permissions_note: For search that follows Confluence permissions, the site must also show user email addresses. Turn this on in admin.atlassian.com, under Settings, User email visibility.

steps.title: Choose the account
steps.text: Use an Atlassian account that can view every space you want synced. For search that follows Confluence permissions, give it Space admin on each of those spaces, and make the site show user email addresses.

steps.title: Create an API token
steps.text: Create an Atlassian API token for that account.

steps.title: Select spaces
steps.text: HydraDB lists the site's spaces. Select the spaces to sync. Each selected space syncs on its own.

connect.account: One connector reads one Confluence Cloud site, as one Atlassian user.

sync.first_sync: Each selected space reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the pages, blog posts and files modified since the last sync, space by space. A newly uploaded file is picked up on its own, without a page edit.
sync.edits: An edited page has a new version, so the next sync reads it again and updates its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted pages and files are not removed. They stay searchable in HydraDB.

shared_attributes.name: updated_at
shared_attributes.text: When the page or file last changed, written as the `Updated` line. Sets the result date.

shared_attributes.name: parent_id
shared_attributes.text: For a page, its parent page, empty at the top of a space. For a file, the page or blog post it is attached to. Links the item to that page. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
shared_attributes.text: The space key, for example `ENG`. Limits a query to one space. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
shared_attributes.text: The space display name. Limits a query to one space by name. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: Space and page restrictions
shared_attributes.text: The space's view permissions and the page's restrictions, including inherited ones. A file uses its page's. Together they decide who can read the item when Enforce ACL is on. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: space
shared_attributes.text: The space display name. To limit a query to a space, use `additional_metadata.container_name`.

shared_attributes.name: space_key
shared_attributes.text: The space key. To limit a query to a space, use `additional_metadata.container_id`.

documents.name: Pages and blog posts
documents.one_document: One page or one blog post.
documents.title: The page or blog post title. One with no title is titled `Confluence content` and its id.
documents.text: The page body with all markup removed. If that leaves nothing, the title is used. The title, author and last-updated time are searchable too. Attached files are separate documents.
documents.date: The time of the page's current version.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The creator's display name, or email if there is no name, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the page as written by that person.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The creator's email, when Confluence shows it. Gives the author an email in the graph, so the same person is recognised across tools. Not searchable.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: People @mentioned in the page, as Confluence usernames or user keys, not display names. The graph records each as mentioned. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.text: The name or email of whoever made the current version. Not attached to the page as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: updated_by_email
attributes.text: That editor's email, when Confluence shows it.

documents.name: Attached files
documents.one_document: One file attached to a page or blog post.
documents.title: The file name. A file with no name is titled `Confluence attachment` and its id.
documents.text: The text read from the file. If no text can be read, the file name is still searchable. The last-modified time is searchable too.
documents.date: When the file was last modified.
documents.files: Each file is downloaded with the connector's credentials. Text from supported attachments is searchable when HydraDB can download and read the files. Only files attached to pages or blog posts are kept. Space logos and template images are left out.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.confluence_page_id
attributes.text: The id of the page the file is attached to. Finds every file on one page. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.confluence_attachment_id
attributes.text: The attachment id. Picks out one file. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.confluence_file_id
attributes.text: The file id, which stays the same across the file's versions. Matches a file across versions. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.confluence_media_type
attributes.text: The file's type, for example `application/pdf`. Limits a query to one file type. Not searchable.

example_searches: What does the ENG space say about our deploy process?
Who wrote the incident postmortem page for the March outage?
What is in the PDFs attached to the Security Policy page?

connections: A page to its parent page.
An attached file to its page or blog post.
No links to items in other tools. A link to another page written in the page text does not become a connection.
people: The creator of each page and blog post.
People @mentioned in a page, by Confluence username or user key.
The editor of the current version is kept with the page but not attached as a person.
graph.from_text: The page text and the text read from attached files. A file is read together with its page's title and text.

not_synced: Spaces the Atlassian account cannot view.
Deletions: deleted pages and files stay in HydraDB.
